title: In Philippians 3 How Can We Actively Pursue A Deeper Relationship With Christ In Our Daily Lives
paragraphs: Pursuing a Deeper Relationship with Christ: Insights from Philippians 3

Philippians 3 offers profound guidance for believers longing to grow closer to Jesus. The apostle Paul, writing from prison, models a passionate pursuit of Christ above all else. This chapter challenges us to consider what it means to know Jesus deeply, not just intellectually, but experientially and personally. Let’s explore how we can actively pursue a deeper relationship with Christ in our daily lives, drawing practical applications and spiritual encouragement from Philippians 3.
1. Value Christ Above All Things
Paul begins by recounting his impressive religious credentials, which, by earthly standards, would make him a spiritual success. Yet he declares:

Yea verily, and I count all things to be loss for the excellency of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord: for whom I suffered the loss of all things, and do count them but refuse, that I may gain Christ, - Philippians 3:8 ASV

Paul’s example teaches us that we must consider all worldly achievements and possessions as “loss” compared to the surpassing worth of knowing Christ. This means examining our hearts daily and asking: What am I treasuring most? What might be competing for my devotion to Jesus?
2. Rely on Christ’s Righteousness, Not Our Own
A key to a deeper relationship with Christ is understanding that our standing before God is not based on our works but on faith in Jesus:

and be found in him, not having a righteousness of mine own, even that which is of the law, but that which is through faith in Christ, the righteousness which is from God by faith: - Philippians 3:9 ASV
This truth frees us from striving to earn God’s favor. We can rest in the righteousness that comes through faith, which encourages us to draw near to Christ daily with confidence and gratitude.
3. Pursue Intimacy with Christ Through Fellowship in Suffering
Paul expresses a longing to know Christ more fully—even through suffering:
that I may know him, and the power of his resurrection, and the fellowship of his sufferings, becoming conformed unto his death; - Philippians 3:10 ASV

While most desire to know the “power of his resurrection,” Paul also embraces the “fellowship of his sufferings.” Trials and hardships, when surrendered to Christ, become opportunities for deeper communion with Him. In our daily struggles, we can ask Jesus to reveal Himself, trusting that He draws near to the brokenhearted (Psalm 34:18 ASV).
4. Press On Toward the Goal
Paul admits he hasn’t arrived, but he presses on:
Not that I have already obtained, or am already made perfect: but I press on, if so be that I may lay hold on that for which also I was laid hold on by Christ Jesus. - Philippians 3:12 ASV

The Christian life is a journey, not a destination. Pursuing Christ involves intentional daily effort—prayer, studying Scripture, worship, and obedience. Paul’s metaphor of pressing on encourages us not to be complacent but to continually seek deeper fellowship with Jesus.
5. Forget What Lies Behind & Reach Forward
Paul’s focus is future-oriented:

forgetting the things which are behind, and stretching forward to the things which are before, I press on toward the goal unto the prize of the high calling of God in Christ Jesus. - Philippians 3:13-14 ASV

To grow closer to Christ, we must let go of past failures, regrets, or even past spiritual victories that might lead to complacency. Instead, we strive each day for a greater experience of God’s presence and purpose.
6. Imitate Mature Believers
Paul invites his readers to follow his example and that of others who walk faithfully:
Brethren, be ye imitators together of me, and mark them that so walk even as ye have us for an ensample. - Philippians 3:17 ASV
Surrounding ourselves with mature Christians and learning from their walk can help us pursue Christ more fervently. Community is essential for encouragement and accountability.
7. Remember Your True Citizenship
Paul concludes with a reminder of our ultimate hope:
For our citizenship is in heaven; whence also we wait for a Saviour, the Lord Jesus Christ: - Philippians 3:20 ASV

Keeping an eternal perspective motivates us to prioritize our relationship with Christ above the temporary things of this world. We live as citizens of heaven, looking forward to seeing Jesus face to face.
Conclusion: Daily Habits for Pursuing Christ
Spend time daily in prayer and Scripture, seeking to know Jesus personally.
Evaluate your priorities—what might you need to count as “loss” to gain Christ?
Invite Jesus into your struggles and joys, seeking to know Him in all circumstances.
Press on, not in your own strength, but relying on the grace and righteousness of Christ.
Engage with mature believers who can encourage and challenge you.
Keep your eyes fixed on your heavenly citizenship and the coming of your Savior.
Growing in intimacy with Christ is the greatest pursuit of the Christian life. May the example of Paul and the truth of Philippians 3 inspire you to seek Jesus wholeheartedly every day.
